newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Military installation bombed in Xinjiang - exiles.
newsitem.headline: Military installation bombed in Xinjiang - exiles.

text.p: A Uighur exile group in Kazakhstan said on Thursday Uighur separatists in China's turbulent northwest province of Xinjiang had carried out a bomb attack against a Chinese military installation.

"The bomb was planted on March 10 in one of the buildings at an arms factory half way between Urumqi and Kashgar," Mukhiddin Mukhlisi, spokesman for the United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
He said buildings were damaged but did not know whether there were any casualties. He said his own organisation was not responsible for the attack.
The Front is one of several Uighur organisations fighting for an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, home to a majority of Turkic-speaking Moslems like the ethnic Uighurs.

In February, rioting between Uighurs and the Chinese authorities broke out in Yining, near Xinjiang's border with the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan. The disturbance was one of the most violent since in the province since the 1949 communist takeover.

Bomb attacks in the regional centre Urumqi and the Chinese capital Beijing followed the unrest in late February and earlier this month. Information from the remote, closed region of mountain and desert is difficult to verify.
